title: Who Owns a Runway Image?
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: Who Owns a Runway Image?: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: A runway image sits inside a stack of interests: the photographed show and garments, the photographer's authorship, any work-made-for-hire status or transfer, model and venue agreements, accreditation terms, licenses, publication rights, and jurisdiction-specific publicity or privacy rules.
frames.alt: Title plate for Who Owns a Runway Image?.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: The image is a distinct authored work around fashion; the clothes, staging, model, commission, publication, and photograph do not collapse into one ownership question.
frames.credit: Toni Frissell Collection, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
frames.alt: Two models wearing evening fashions in a 1956 Toni Frissell photograph made for Sports Illustrated.
frames.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set
frames.treatment: local display and download with attached credit

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · AUTHOR — Who made the photograph?. Record the photographer, capture date and time, file origin, embedded metadata, assignment, employer, commissioning party, and whether a statutory work-made-for-hire theory is actually supported. Payment alone is not the test.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who made the photograph? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · TRANSFER — Did ownership or an exclusive right move?. Locate the signed writing, identify the rights transferred, territory, media, duration, exclusivity, sublicensing, credit, editing, archive, and termination terms. A delivery folder, invoice, or social post may be relevant evidence but is not automatically a complete transfer instrument.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping did ownership or an exclusive right move? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · PERMISSION STACK — What else governs use?. Separate copyright from accreditation terms, publication license, model agreement, venue rules, embargo, trademark presentation, publicity or privacy law, and contractual restrictions. The answer may change with use, territory, and audience.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what else governs use? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · PUBLISH — Can the exact use be shown?. Before publishing, bind the exact image or clip to its source record, permitted use, crop or edit, credit, caption, alt text, license evidence, expiration, takedown route, and counsel decision where the stack remains uncertain.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping can the exact use be shown? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: A permissions system can become so risk-averse that it erases photographers, models, and makers from public memory. The answer is not casual reuse; it is better licensing, clearer credits, fairer agreements, durable records, and a proportionate review process that preserves access without laundering uncertainty.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for Who Owns a Runway Image?.
